articles.title: This is my biggest AirPods complaint, and it’s not necessarily about the hardware
articles.summary: AirPods are one of Apple’s most interesting products. The demand for them was largely invented by the fact that the company removed the headphone jack 10 years ago, and now most of us carry this almost magical pair of earbuds that do so much more than just play audio. AirPods offer best-in-class noise cancellation, and also serve as a hearing aid. They get better and better almost every year. Despite everything that AirPods do so well, I have one annoyance with them, and it’s particularly annoying because it could be such an easy software fix. more…

articles.title: Fitbit Edge leaks in full: Google’s new fitness tracker finally spills its secrets
articles.summary: TL;DR An upcoming Google wearable called the ‘Fitbit Edge’ has leaked in full. It is reportedly a new Fitbit Air-like fitness band, albeit with a small screen and support for a limited set of apps, such as Google Maps and YouTube Music. The device is expected to feature up to seven days of battery life, GPS, an altimeter, and support for displaying notifications. Google is reportedly getting ready to launch a new Fitbit fitness tracker that sits between the Fitbit Air and the Pixel Watch 5 . According to a tell-all leak from Android Headlines , the device is called the Fitbit Edge, and exclusive images give us our first detailed look at what could be Fitbit’s next screen-equipped tracker.

articles.title: New forensic evidence supports Egyptian "retainer sacrifice"
articles.summary: Egyptologists have long debated whether the earliest pharoahs of the First Dynasty were buried with various servants and officials to serve them in the afterlife—a form of human sacrifice . But there is very little archaeological evidence available, given that many of the earliest Egyptian tombs were plundered and/or hastily excavated. A new paper published in the journal Frontiers in Environmental Archaeology reassesses a collection of skulls excavated from tombs in the 1920s and concludes that over one-third show evidence of blunt force trauma. This suggests that they may have been victims of so-called "retainer sacrifice." articles.title: 蘋果將增加macOS完全磁碟存取的開關控制
articles.summary:
由於Meta Muse for macOS有擅自存取用戶電腦資料的疑慮，蘋果上周宣布將為macOS增加完全磁碟存取（Full Disk Access）的開關控制，以防使用者資料被App暗中存取。
Meta於9月初公布個人助理App Muse。這個個人助理號稱可協助用戶發送郵件、預訂旅程、購物或管理跨步驟的長期任務。但它只會在取得用戶同意或授權後才會執行。

articles.title: Cloudflare開源Clef決策模型，主打快速判斷並整合Workers AI
articles.summary:
Cloudflare推出自行訓練的決策模型Clef與Clef-flash，兩款模型已整合至Workers AI，並以Apache 2.0授權開放模型權重。Clef採用與Jev相容的程式介面，既有使用Jev的應用較容易改用Clef，主要用於AI代理進行分類、判斷或決定下一步動作。
決策模型和一般大型語言模型負責的工作不同，大型語言模型可以產生文字、進行推理或操作工具，決策模型則專門處理範圍明確的判斷。開發者先設定可接受的答案，模型讀取輸入資料後，直接回傳符合指定格式的答案及各選項機率。

articles.summary: 微軟最新全球網路威脅觀察指出，AI正加快漏洞研究、惡意程式開發及入侵後的攻擊活動。漏洞從實際環境中被發現到遭武器化，中位時間已縮短至遠低於24小時；企業修補重大對外漏洞則可能需要30至60天。過去6個月，攻擊者不只利用AI協助執行攻擊，也開始讓AI協調不同攻擊步驟，朝自主執行網路攻擊發展。

articles.title: Backside Clock Meshes Cut Skew and Power in 2nm Nanosheets (UCSC)
articles.summary: Researchers at the University of California, Santa Cruz published a technical paper titled “Design Space Exploration of Backside Clock Meshes for 2 nm GAAFET BSPDN Technology.” Abstract Excerpt: “Clock meshes are used in high-performance VLSI designs to minimize skew and tolerate on-chip variation, but they spend scarce routing resources on premium metal layers. Backside power delivery creates a new option: it adds thick, low-resistance metal layers on the back of the wafer, and the power grid does not consume all of them. Flip-flops remain on the frontside; a backside mesh therefore cannot drive them directly, and every connection passes through a through-silicon via. articles.title: Extreme Environments Push Chips To Their Breaking Point
articles.summary: Key Takeaways: Orbital data centers, military/aerospace vehicles, HPC experiments, quantum, and advanced manufacturing equipment are all putting pressure on chips to withstand extreme environments. Conditions include any combination of thermal and mechanical shock, radiation, high speeds, noise, vibration, pressure, and humidity. Advanced 4D modeling, simulation, AI/LLM-based design exploration, and physical lab tools are all needed to ensure complex chips and systems can survive. articles.title: Want cheaper flights? Google says this is the best time to book one
articles.summary: TL;DR Google says domestic flights have historically been cheapest around 39 days before departure, while international fares hit their lowest around 89 days out. The idea that Tuesday is the best day to book is largely a myth, with the cheapest booking day saving only about 1.4% versus the most expensive. Changing when and how you fly matters more: weekday travel can save up to 20% domestically, while nonstop flights cost around 20% more than connecting options. articles.title: Android Auto could soon stop working on millions of phones
articles.summary: TL;DR Users on Android 10 are starting to receive warnings that Android Auto will soon stop working on their phones. The alerts suggest Google may be preparing to raise the minimum Android Auto requirement for wired connections to Android 11. Google hasn’t announced the change yet, and its support pages still list Android 9 Pie as the minimum for wired Android Auto. Android Auto has already left several older versions of Android behind over the years, and another cutoff now appears to be approaching. Google dropped support for Android 8 Oreo and older devices in 2022, then moved the minimum to Android 9 Pie in 2024 . Now, Android 10 users are starting to see warnings that their phones will soon stop working with Android Auto, suggesting Android 11 could become the next minimum requirement.

articles.title: We’re witnessing a critical moment for Amazon Kindles
articles.summary: Credit: Amazon To say that Amazon has had a rough year with the Kindle would be an understatement. Between sunsetting older e-reader models, making it harder to download purchased Kindle books, and introducing a series of changes that gave power users plenty to complain about, Amazon’s Kindle ecosystem was clearly going through a rough patch. It’s gotten to a point where plenty of users have started looking at Kobo or one of the many Android-powered e-readers instead. These alternatives offer many of the extras that Kindle fans have been asking for for years – physical buttons, support for more formats, and better customization. Basically, they offer more control over the device you paid for.

articles.title: GrapheneOS explains why your Pixel is lagging and freezing after Android 17 QPR1
articles.summary: TL;DR Some Pixel owners reported worse performance after installing September’s Android 17 QPR1 update. GrapheneOS says it has found a regression in the update that can cause lag, stuttering, freezes, and app crashes under memory pressure. While GrapheneOS has already patched the problem, stock Pixel users are still waiting for Google to release a fix. Android 17 QPR1 was supposed to improve Pixel phones, but for a noticeable number of owners, the September update seems to have had the opposite effect. We recently asked Android Authority readers how their Pixels were behaving after installing the update , and performance problems stood out as the most common complaint among those who reported new issues. Now, GrapheneOS may have finally found the reason for at least some of that slowdown.

articles.title: Connecting AI agents to enterprise knowledge
articles.summary: For all the data that AI systems continually amass and analyze, enterprise AI agents often suffer from a curious shortcoming: a lack of knowledge. More than data, knowledge is the understanding of what the data means in the context of individual organizations. AI agents need this understanding to reason about situations, make decisions, and ultimately take actions. Without sufficient knowledge, agents are prone to making flawed and unreliable decisions. A lack of knowledge, our research finds, is a major reason agentic AI use cases never make it to production. Competitive pressure is making it urgent to address this. articles.title: Bringing predictive analytics to the agentic AI era
articles.summary: In 2026, the question for enterprise AI is no longer whether predictive models can outperform statistical forecasts—that argument is settled. The big question now is how to enable predictive systems to act on their own conclusions without drifting from business intent. The frontier has moved from prediction to autonomous decision making, and the gap between leaders and laggards is widening accordingly. “Enterprises are done with a backward-looking point of view; they want to be more forward-thinking,” says Vishal Gupta, partner at research firm Everest Group. articles.title: People really hate AI, so why can’t they get enough?
articles.summary: Over the summer I talked to the CEO of Springboards, a startup building an LLM that’s designed to come up with a wider variety of responses than its mainstream rivals do. At the start of the call, he said something that’s been stuck in my head since: “We often say that we’re a self-loathing AI company. We don’t know if we really like what we’re doing.” “I guess that makes me a self-loathing AI journalist,” I replied. It was a joke! I love my job. But I do not love many of the things the technology I write about has become: warped by hype , steered by zealots , inescapable . The CEO of Springboards and I are far from alone. Around the world, a love/hate attitude toward AI is very much the vibe right now. On the one hand, public feelings are souring fast. According to the Pew Research Center

articles.title: OpenAI brings text watermarking to its API — and unlike Anthropic, it’s off by default
articles.summary: OpenAI has announced that developers can now opt in to watermarking text generated through its API, as the company extends its existing content provenance efforts to one of the more difficult forms of AI output to reliably identify. In a blog post published on Monday , the company details a new system dubbed textGrain, which embeds a “statistical signal” into generated text by subtly influencing the words a model chooses — for example, favoring one suitable word over another when either would make sense in a sentence. Over a long enough passage, those choices form a pattern that OpenAI’s detector can identify. API customers worldwide can enable watermarking on supported models from today, and in the coming weeks, OpenAI says it will begin automatically watermarking

articles.title: Dynatrace’s $915M Arize deal bets AI agents are just another app to monitor
articles.summary: Dynatrace closed its $915 million acquisition of Arize on October 1 , joining Arize’s tracing and evaluation of AI agents to its own monitoring of the applications and infrastructure underneath them. It also takes an independent AI observability vendor off the market, one Datadog had invested in. I sat down with Sean O’Dell , a principal product marketing manager at Dynatrace , on September 25 at the WeAreDevelopers conference in San Jose, five days before the deal closed. Dynatrace was in a quiet period, so he kept his Arize comments general. When I asked where Dynatrace is headed with Arize, his answer started from the premise that an AI app is still an app. When it breaks, the business needs to know what the outage cost, and the engineers on call need to know why it happened

articles.summary: Guardrail selection has typically meant choosing between a purpose-built classifier and an LLM acting as a judge. Decision models such as TypeSafe AI’s Jev have added a third option, promising the flexibility of zero-shot policies without the cost of open-ended generation. TypeSafe launched Jev in mid-September with performance claims based on evaluations it designed and ran itself. Red Hat’s AI Safety team has now put all three approaches through the same benchmarks . It tested nine guardrail configurations on prompt injection and content safety, running each through NVIDIA’s open source NeMo Guardrails toolkit. And the first result was actually pretty close. articles.title: XCOR launches to trace outages in minutes. It still pages engineers.
articles.summary: Palo Alto Networks introduced a new approach to AI-driven observability last week, signaling a shift from dashboards and manual incident response toward AI agents that investigate issues and recommend fixes on their own. Cortex XCOR is an AI-driven platform designed to deliver the holy grail of observability: automatically root-causing issues and recommending fixes, rather than simply pointing technical operatives to dashboards. The company has said the foundational scale and cost challenges of cloud-native architectures stood in the way of this happening before now, and pre-AI-boom automation was sluggish. articles.title: 'Blue Horseshoe': Tracking 'Big Active'
articles.summary: Scarlet Fu and Eric Balchunas discuss the new Bloomberg Intelligence tool 'Blue Horseshoe' on "Bloomberg ETF IQ." The new "Blue Horseshoe" tool lets Bloomberg Terminal users see which stocks the biggest active managers ('Big Active') are buying and selling every day on an aggregate basis. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: AI Spending Rolls On as Tech Wealth Hits Records
articles.summary: Companies are spending billions on AI, but actually getting it into production remains a major challenge. Insight Partners sees forward-deployed engineers as part of the solution: embedding directly with customers to turn AI into working products and workflows. Insight Partners Operating Partner Pablo Dominguez joins to discuss why the firm is launching a dedicated practice to help its portfolio companies build that capability. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: AI ‘Pacing’ Doesn’t Mean Slower Adoption
articles.summary: NEA partner Tiffany Luck says any slowdown in development at the AI frontier doesn’t have to slow adoption across the economy. She argues increasingly powerful models from OpenAI, Anthropic and others are already well ahead of enterprise deployment, leaving a major opportunity for companies that can turn raw intelligence into real-world workflows and measurable returns. She joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.title: CH Robinson to Buy RXO for $5.8B in Bet on AI Model
articles.summary: CH Robinson agreed to buy trucking brokerage firm RXO Inc. in a deal centered around a bet that artificial intelligence can help the companies improve efficiency in a challenging freight market. Through a cash-and-stock transaction valued at about $5.8 billion, CH Robinson aims to diversify its business and capitalize on RXO’s abilities in expedited and last-mile delivery. CH Robinson, which has been using AI to transform its operations to become leaner, intends to use the system to extract $300 million of cost savings within two years. Lee Klaskow, Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Transport, Logistics and Shipping Analyst says that the $300 million estimate could be conservative. (Source: Bloomberg)

articles.summary: Maggie Fanari, chief executive officer of J. Rothschild Capital Management and an Anthropic investor, says the AI company can continue creating value after going public as it compounds growth over the long term. articles.title: Controlling the brain with light earns a physiology Nobel
articles.summary: Over decades of research, scientists have built up a partial picture of what specialized cells within the brain and spinal cord do. By studying how the brain develops, they could identify genes that were active in different populations of neurons and where in the brain those neurons resided. In some cases, these genes could then be used to genetically delete the neurons, allowing us to get some indication of what they might be doing, building on the information we've obtained from studies of brains with damaged regions. But this approach has its limits. articles.title: AI glasses face their first major government crackdown
articles.summary: Norway has become the first major country to propose a temporary ban on the use of AI glasses in selected public places amid growing privacy concerns over wearable technology. The rich Scandinavian country’s center-left government said on Monday that it would introduce a law to parliament soon on a temporary ban for places such as parks, beaches, schools, and kindergartens. It will also set up an expert group to propose permanent national rules. “I am concerned about the introduction of powerful new technology where people risk being photographed, filmed, or recorded without their knowledge,” said Torgeir Micaelsen, Norway’s digitalization minister. articles.title: Explaining Hall-effect, TMR, and other new types of "mechanical" switches
articles.summary: The mechanical keyboard isn't always so mechanical anymore. Over the past six years, keyboards with optical, Hall-effect, and other "contactless" switches have become increasingly common, often going for higher prices than traditional mechanical keyboards, which already command a premium over basic membrane boards. In return, they promise some theoretical advantages, particularly for gamers. In daily use, though, the differences can be pretty subtle. So what exactly are you paying for? In this guide, we break down how the newest switches work, why contactless designs are becoming more popular, and where their advantages—and disadvantages—really matter. Read full article Comments

articles.title: AI資料中心擴建爭議升高，Amazon加碼逾10億美元回應地方疑慮
articles.summary: Amazon公布新的資料中心營運與社區承諾，回應近期資料中心擴建引發的電力、用水及地方社區疑慮。未來5年將在美國資料中心所在地額外投入超過10億美元，用於教育、職業訓練及能源與用水改善，Amazon也表示，今後不再與資料中心專案合作的政府機關簽署保密協議，並將每年公開能源與用水等營運資料。

articles.title: Anthropic投入1億美元培訓萬名工程師，強化企業Claude部署能力
articles.summary: Anthropic周五（10/2）宣布推出Claude Frontier Academy，並投入1億美元培訓企業AI人才，目標在2027年底前培養1萬名前線部署工程師（Frontier Deployed Engineers，FDE），協助企業將Claude導入實際工作流程與正式生產環境。首批學員來自Accenture、Bain、Capgemini、Deloitte、McKinsey、Morgan Stanley、Novo Nordisk及澳洲聯邦銀行等企業。
